{{nihongo|'''Hiroaki Kitano'''|北野 宏明|extra=born 1961 in [[Tokyo]]}} is a Japanese [[scientist]], head of the [[Systems Biology Institute]], Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Technology Officer of the [[Sony]] Group Corporation, Chief Executive Officer of Sony Research Inc. and Sony Computer Science Laboratories, Inc.;<ref name="Message from CTO">{{cite web|title=Sony Group Portal - Message from CTO|url=https://www.sony.com/en/SonyInfo/technology/message/|access-date=10 October 2023|archive-date=10 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231010114244/https://www.sony.com/en/SonyInfo/technology/message/}}</ref> a Group Director of the Laboratory for Disease Systems Modeling at and [[RIKEN]] Center for Integrative Medical Sciences; and a professor at [[Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology]] (OIST).<ref name=sbi-members>{{cite web|title=The Systems Biology Institute: Members|url=http://www.sbi.jp/members.htm|website=sbi.jp|access-date=5 September 2014|archive-date=21 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141021142335/http://www.sbi.jp/members.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> Kitano is known for developing [[AIBO]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Robots |url=http://www.businessweek.com/magazine/content/01_12/b3724007.htm|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120729090713/http://www.businessweek.com/magazine/content/01_12/b3724007.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=29 July 2012|access-date=2 January 2011|newspaper=[[Business Week]]|date=19 March 2001|author=Irene M. Kunii|author2=Otis Port}}</ref> and the robotic world cup tournament known as [[Robocup]].<ref name="robocup"/><ref>{{cite news|title=World Cup robot competition to kick off in Germany|url=http://www.itworld.com/060612robocup|access-date=2 January 2011|newspaper=IT World|date=12 June 2006}}</ref>

==Education==
Kitano graduated from [[International Christian University]] with a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in physics in 1984. He received a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in computer science from [[Kyoto University]] in 1991.<ref name=cv>{{cite web|title=CV: Hiroaki Kitano|url=http://www.jst.go.jp/sicp/ws2009_se2nd/cv/05_kitano.pdf|website=jst.go.jp|access-date=5 September 2014}}</ref> His PhD thesis in [[machine translation]] was titled "Speech-to-speech translation: a massively parallel memory-based approach".  His work includes a broad spectrum of publications in artificial intelligence and interactomics.

==Research==
From 1988 to 1994, Kitano was a visiting researcher at the Center for Machine Translation at [[Carnegie Mellon University]].<ref name=keynote-cv>{{cite web|title=KEYNOTE SPEAKERS - 35th Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society|url=http://embc2013.embs.org/keynote_speakers.html|website=embc2013.embs.org|access-date=5 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150323223238/http://embc2013.embs.org/keynote_speakers.html|archive-date=23 March 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

At Sony, Kitano started the development of the [[AIBO]] robotic pet. This research was developed further as the [[QRIO]], a bipedal humanoid robot.<ref name=icsb14>{{cite web|title=Hiroaki Kitano - The 15th International Conference on Systems Biology 2014|url=http://www.icsb14.com/pages/hiroaki-kitano-.php|website=icsb14.com|access-date=5 September 2014|archive-date=5 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140905150146/http://www.icsb14.com/pages/hiroaki-kitano-.php|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=kirainet>{{cite web|title=Hiroaki Kitano's dream Kirainet - A geek in Japan|url=http://www.kirainet.com/english/hiroaki-kitanos-dream/|website=kirainet.com|access-date=5 September 2014|archive-date=5 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140905151403/http://www.kirainet.com/english/hiroaki-kitanos-dream/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The research behind AIBO and QRIO led to Kitano founding the [[RoboCup]] annual international robotics competition in 1997. The goal of RoboCup is to create a team of autonomous robotic footballers that would be able to beat the best team in the world, by 2050.<ref name=icsb14 /><ref name=kirainet /><ref name=robocup-objective>{{cite web|url=http://www.robocup.org/about-robocup/objective/|title=RoboCup: Objective|publisher=RoboCup|year=1998|access-date=2014-01-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140104080054/http://www.robocup.org/about-robocup/objective/|archive-date=4 January 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Kitano has made significant contributions to [[Systems biology]], including a contribution to the [[Systems Biology Markup Language]] (SBML).<ref>{{Cite journal| first1 = H.| title = Systems biology: a brief overview| journal = Science| volume = 295| issue = 5560| pages = 1662–1664| last1 = Kitano| year = 2002| pmid = 11872829| doi = 10.1126/science.1069492      |bibcode = 2002Sci...295.1662K | s2cid = 2703843| url = http://theory.bio.uu.nl/BPA/pdf/Obligatory_reading/Kitano_s02.pdf}}</ref><ref name="pmid12611808">{{Cite journal

==Roles and awards==
Kitano has served as a scientific advisor for a number of companies, including [[Alstom]], [[Segway Inc.|Segway]] Japan and [[Mitsubishi Chemical Holdings]]. He was awarded the [[IJCAI Computers and Thought Award]] in 1993 and the [[Nature Publishing Group|Nature]] Award for Creative Mentoring in Science in 2009.<ref name=whs-cv>{{cite web|title=140602 Kitano_Hiroaki_CV|url=http://www.worldhealthsummit.org/fileadmin/downloads/2014/WHS/CV/140602%20Kitano_Hiroaki_CV.pdf|website=worldhealthsummit.org|access-date=5 September 2014}}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence]] in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Elected AAAI Fellows |url=https://aaai.org/about-aaai/aaai-awards/the-aaai-fellows-program/elected-aaai-fellows/ |access-date=2024-01-03 |website=AAAI |language=en-US}}</ref>
